name: guess the output size, run an output-sensitive procedure against it, and square the guess on failure
mechanism: run a procedure whose cost depends on an assumed output size (here: hull the input in groups of that size, then wrap over the group hulls for that many steps); if the output is not finished within the guess, square the guess and start over; the doubling-of-exponents makes the total cost proportional to the final successful run

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Chan's algorithm' in section Computational mathematics / Geometry:

requires: an inner procedure whose cost is controlled by the guess
fails_when: the wasted runs are cheap only because the guess grows so fast
